about: The findings of e2e/test-timing-check.mjs that stay for now: those present when the check was added at 86db135, and those its later rules found at 0295880. Rule 1 of docs/review-standards.md (on its branch, PR 339).

Reviewed like code. An entry matches by file, rule, where (the enclosing test's title path, or the enclosing function's name) and the exact text of its line, and must match exactly `count` findings (1 if absent). A new copy of an allowed line, an entry re-pointed at the same text elsewhere, an entry whose line changed, or one with no reason, no where, no category from below, or no `owed` fails the check.

`calls_allowed: true` allows every call to the helper the entry's sleep is in, and only an entry with `owed: false` may say it (a poll, or a stand-in's own failure bound). A call to any other helper that sleeps is its own finding and its own entry, so a new one fails.
`owed: true` is a debt, with what it needs written in its reason; `owed: false` is right as it is. Every run prints the number owed.
`lines_when_listed` and `listed_at` are for a reader: the check doesn't use them, and lines move.
The fixes land one category per PR, removing entries as they go: R (rooms), then I and J (margins), then B's four API cases and E.

categories.A: sleep: a bounded poll for the state itself (right as it is, unless its reason says owed)
categories.B: sleep: a wait, then an assertion that nothing happened
categories.C: sleep: so a streaming request is in flight before the test acts
categories.D: sleep: a few milliseconds so the clock moves on
categories.E: sleep: a fixed run of passes, then exact counts
categories.F: sleep: real time for a back-off to run out
categories.G: sleep: for a third-party agent's run
categories.H: sleep: a stand-in's pacing in the safe direction (right as it is)
categories.I: margin: a lower bound read after the action
categories.J: margin: an upper bound read before the action
categories.K: margin: a fixed bound after the action, safe only by the order of a stamp and a reading
categories.R: unquieted: an API spec that makes rooms and quiets none
categories.S: sleep: a stand-in's own bound that only detects a failure (right as it is)

known_gaps.what: "stops after a strict number across all clients": a fixed counter (STRICT_COUNTER) other tests' sign-ups also count against.
known_gaps.why_unseen: No rule here can see a shared counter's name; found in PR 342's review.

known_gaps.what: "takes five a minute per client": counts on a fixed client name within a wall-clock minute, which can roll over mid-test, and which other tests' traffic under the same name adds to.
known_gaps.why_unseen: A rate limit's window and key name aren't a sleep or a margin; found in PR 342's review.

entries.where: an offer to an agent > goes on the A2A queue holding IDs only
entries.reason: A poll for the state itself: the loop re-reads it, stops as soon as it is there, and throws or is followed by an expect when the bound runs out. The timer only paces the re-reads, and the bound only detects a failure. Owed: it waits up to 5 s (100 tries, 50 ms apart) for the queue send that follows the offer asynchronously, and a loaded runner can take longer. What would remove the wait: hold the send at the stand-in's queue hook and await its arrival there.

It holds only because queued_at is normally stamped before `after` is read, and the 5 s is a margin a late stamp could use up. What would remove it: bracket queued_at between readings taken before and after the action, with no number added.

entries.where: function passGate
entries.code: const expiry = new Promise<void>((resolve) => { timer = setTimeout(() => { gate.expired = true; resolve(); }, GATE_LIMIT_MS); });
entries.reason: A gate's own limit: it answers a call the test forgot to release after 2 s and marks the gate expired, so the test sees it and fails. A failure detector, never a pass condition.

entries.where: function unanswered
entries.reason: Holds a call until the caller gives up, so "no answer in time" never rests on this side's clock; 60 s is only an end for a request nobody aborts, and nobody reads what follows.

entries.where: function takeFault
entries.code: if (fault.delayMs) await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, fault.delayMs));
entries.reason: A fault's scripted delay (delayMs): a test that scripts one may pass only because the delay is longer or shorter than the caller's wait. Owed: find the tests that script a delay and replace each with a hold the test releases (as the gates do).
